uncited: It differs from [First-order Spherical Harmonics Distillation](9467-first-order-spherical-harmonics-distillation.md) by retaining full SH basis functions (rather than reducing to first-order) and from [Explicit Camera Jacobian Derivation](10077-explicit-camera-jacobian-derivation.md) by focusing on storage compression rather than gradient computation.
It is chosen when memory bandwidth or storage size is the primary bottleneck and view-dependent specular effects must be preserved better than simple color quantization allows.

*   **Input:** A set of $N$ Gaussian splats, each with a view-dependent color defined by SH coefficients $\mathbf{c}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{45}$ (excluding the zeroth-order term, which is treated as base color).

*   **Output:** A palette $\mathcal{P} \in \mathbb{R}^{K \times 45}$ of $K$ distinct SH vectors, and an index array $\mathbf{I} \in \mathbb{Z}^{N}$ where $\mathbf{I}[i]$ is the index into $\mathcal{P}$ for splat $i$.
Each vector contains 45 floating-point numbers (15 per RGB channel).
Each integer is 16 bits wide, capable of addressing up to 65,536 palette entries.
**Extract SH Data:** Collect the 45-dimensional SH coefficient vector for every splat in the scene, excluding the 0th-order coefficient.
**Cluster:** Perform vector quantization (clustering) on the $N$ data points in $\mathbb{R}^{45}$ to find $K$ cluster centers.
*   *Note:* Standard k-means is too slow for millions of splats in 45 dimensions.
It was developed as part of a toy "Gaussian Splatting for Unity" implementation to enable efficient real-time rendering of large scenes on constrained hardware.
